analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only file. The changed ranges are the date bump on line 3, GLM5-Next video wording near lines 810-813 and 829, a new paragraph near 876-880, and lines 1717-1726, a native-tracked engine paragraph. Units 12 and 13 cover lines 1215-2035. Only 1717-1726 falls inside the supplied excerpt. The other changed ranges are outside the supplied units and were only seen as patch context.

Lines 1717-1726 describe EngineV2Bridge.nativeOutputControlRefusal. A native-tracked engine (GLM5-Next, MiMo V2.6) now rejects topLogprobs rows and token constraints before any reservation, as a 400 invalid_request with reason client_error. Before this, such requests reached submit and surfaced as a 500 generation_failure, which counts against the coordinator's inference-error breaker. The change is described as moving a consumer-triggerable error from the provider-fault class to the client-error class. That matches the availability intent of TB-002 and T-010. It limits a malicious consumer's (ADV-002) ability to trip the breaker against a provider.

The documented control lives in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/Bridge/EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift. That source is not supplied, so the claimed behavior is unverified. Nothing in the excerpt shows a weakened control. The text does not touch the encryption, attestation, authorization or prefix-cache boundaries (T-041, T-053, T-054). It does not alter the SEC-035 accepted-risk posture or any threat-model assertion.

The doc claims that the VFR-video refusal for GLM5-Next media is removed, with frames indexed by nominal frame rate. That change is outside the supplied units, so it was not reviewed for a decode-resource or DoS effect. The doc states that decoded-frame caps (512 MiB) and the prepared-pixel cap remain. A later pass could check that the code matches this before it is trusted.

No security regression or new attack surface is shown in the supplied evidence, and no finding qualifies. Reviewing the source for the native output-control refusal and the VFR video handling remains useful.
